topic: The Mahjong Mirror's Third Angle applied to love. Identifying the real opposition in a relationship, including the Peach Blossom and Sword tiles, and three questions for working through relational blocks.
phrases: The Mirror doesn't soften what it shows.
Name the opposition before it names you.
What are we not saying to each other?

images.concept: An ornate hand mirror lying face-up on dark aged wood, its surface reflecting a single candle flame. The mirror as a tool of honest reflection, not decoration. The image captures the idea of looking clearly at what's there, even when it's uncomfortable.
images.card: Mirror (Guardian category). The reflective surface is the hero element.
images.prompt: An ornate antique hand mirror laid flat face-up on dark, aged hardwood. Its surface reflects the flame of a single beeswax candle standing just out of frame. The mirror frame is cast brass with gentle floral detail, warm antique gold, slightly tarnished. Around the mirror: scattered dried rose petals, a folded letter left unread. The candlelight is warm and singular, creating long shadows across the wood grain. Overhead shot from about 45 degrees. Midnight jade shadows, antique gold light, warm ivory parchment tones. The overall feeling is intimacy, honesty, and the quiet courage it takes to look at something clearly. Cinematic. No text. No watermarks or Western zodiac imagery anywhere in the image.

images.concept: Two Mahjong tiles face-up on dark silk: the Peach Blossom tile and the Sword tile side by side. The contrast between them tells the whole story: temptation vs. clarity, passion vs. decisiveness. This is the first and only tile reference in this week's imagery.
images.card: Peach Blossom (Love, Appendix) and Sword (Opposition indicator)
images.prompt: Two Mahjong tiles placed side by side on dark midnight jade silk. The left tile has a delicate peach blossom motif, feminine and intricate, rendered in dusty rose and antique gold on aged ivory. The right tile bears a sword motif, clean and decisive, rendered in deep plum and antique gold. Candlelight from the upper right, casting warm light across both tiles with contrasting shadows. The tiles are photographed at a slight angle, not perfectly flat, giving them three-dimensional weight. They feel ancient and meaningful, not decorative. No additional objects. The composition is simple and strong. No text. No watermarks or Western zodiac imagery anywhere in the image.

images.concept: A woman standing before a large mirror in a dimly lit room, her silhouette visible but her face turned away. The image of someone looking honestly at their own reflection. The mirror reflects something slightly different from what's expected, suggesting the honest view the Third Angle provides.
images.prompt: Square composition. A woman in her thirties stands in front of a large, floor-length ornate mirror in a dimly lit room. She is seen from slightly behind and to the side, never facing the camera. Her reflection in the mirror shows her face in profile, expression thoughtful and unguarded. The mirror frame is dark wood with antique gold detail. A single candle burns on a shelf to her left. The room behind her falls into soft shadow. The scene feels private, as if caught in a moment of genuine self-examination. Warm ivory and antique gold light on the woman. Midnight jade shadow in the room. Cinematic film still quality. No text. No watermarks or Western zodiac imagery anywhere in the image.

images.concept: A cracked ceramic vase, still beautiful, holding dried flowers. The visual metaphor for a relationship under pressure: still standing, still holding something, but the fracture visible if you look closely. The image carries the idea of honest assessment before things break completely.
images.prompt: A wide cinematic shot of a ceramic vase on a window ledge, early morning light from the left. The vase is pale ivory with a visible hairline crack running from rim to base. The crack is not hidden; it's simply part of the object. Inside the vase: a small arrangement of dried peony heads, dusty rose. The window beyond is slightly out of focus, warm light filtering through. The composition is quiet and still. The crack is neither dramatized nor ignored. It simply is what it is. Antique gold morning light, warm ivory, dusty rose, soft sage. No text. No watermarks or Western zodiac imagery anywhere in the image.

images.concept: Close-up of the two Mahjong tiles (Peach Blossom and Sword) for Instagram. Tighter crop than the Facebook version, more intimate. The texture of the tiles and the candlelight should feel like you're in the room with them.
images.card: Peach Blossom (Love, Appendix) and Sword (Opposition indicator)
images.prompt: Square tight close-up of two Mahjong tiles on dark midnight jade silk, seen nearly from above at a slight angle. The tiles fill most of the frame. Left tile: a peach blossom motif in dusty rose and antique gold on aged ivory. Right tile: a sword motif in deep plum and antique gold. A single candle flame is visible at the upper right edge of the frame, casting warm directional light. The tiles are large enough to see the detail of the surface: the slight wear at the edges, the patina of age. The background silk is dark and textured. The overall feeling is intimate and weighty. These are objects that carry meaning. No text. No watermarks or Western zodiac imagery anywhere in the image.
